desc:
An unmaintained WordPress site slowly becomes slower, less safe and harder to fix. Ecom Swift LLC provides a one-off starter round of WordPress maintenance and security care: backups, tested updates, security checks and clean-up.

## What is WordPress maintenance and security care?

WordPress maintenance is the routine work that keeps a site healthy: taking backups, updating WordPress core, themes and plugins, checking for broken pages, clearing spam and closing security gaps. Security care is the part of that work that reduces the chance of someone breaking in or the site failing without warning.

Our package is a fixed starter sprint. It is not a subscription. If you want the same care every month, we quote that separately.

## Why sites need regular care

WordPress is open software, and it is updated often. Plugin and theme makers release fixes, some of them for security problems. A site that skips those updates for months becomes a target, because known weaknesses are public.

The opposite problem is just as real. Owners who press every update button on a live site risk breaking a page or a form. Safe maintenance means taking a backup first, trying updates on a copy and checking the result before touching the live site.

## What good maintenance does for you

The benefit is mostly the problems that do not happen. A recent backup means a mistake or a hacked site can be restored. Updated software closes known holes. Fewer plugins mean fewer things to go wrong and less code to load, so pages tend to respond faster.

It also protects your reputation. Visitors who land on an error page or a warning from their browser may not return. Time saved matters as well, since a planned round of care is cheaper than an emergency repair.

## What a proper maintenance round includes

- A complete backup of your files and database, taken before we touch anything.
- Updates to WordPress core, your theme and every plugin, tried on a staging copy first.
- A check of key pages and forms after the updates.
- A broken link and missing page scan.
- Malware and vulnerability checks, with repairs for any issues discovered.
- Removal of unused or abandoned plugins.
- Login protection, such as limits on repeated failed attempts.
- Scheduled automatic backups saved off the site.
- Spam comments and junk entries cleared.
- A short report of what was done and what to watch.

## How the sprint works

We begin with a backup so there is always a way back. Then we copy the site to a staging area, run the updates there and test pages, menus and forms. When everything works, we apply the same updates to the live site.

Basic covers the backup, updates, link check and spam clean-up. Standard adds the security sweep, plugin clean-up, login protection and scheduled backups. Premium adds database tidying, speed fixes on the most visited pages, an uptime alert, a few small content fixes and a period of follow-up help. Add-ons include a malware scan report and a quote for monthly care.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep a backup stored outside your hosting account.
- Update on a staging copy when the site matters to your income.
- Remove plugins you no longer use, rather than only turning them off.
- Use strong, unique passwords and a login limit.
- Read the report and act on the notes.

**Avoid:**
- Running every update on the live site without a backup.
- Keeping old themes and plugins that never get updates.
- Sharing one login among several people.
- Ignoring warnings from your host.
- Assuming a security plugin replaces updates.

## Who it is for

Owners who built a site years ago and have not touched it since will see the most difference. Businesses that depend on the site for enquiries or sales and cannot afford downtime also benefit. So do owners who took over a site from a previous developer and are unsure of its state.

## How to get started

Send your site address and tell us who hosts it. We need an administrator invitation in WordPress and, where required, access to your hosting dashboard, given as a collaborator or developer user. We never ask for passwords. Tell us about any plugin you know is sensitive, such as a booking or payment tool, so we test it carefully.
